item.title: Could a Cannabis Maze Be Michigan
item.description: As Minnesota debuts the country’s first haunted cannabis maze, could Michigan follow suit? With its thriving cannabis industry, Michigan may be well-suited for this new fall attraction.

item.title: Mason Residents to Vote on Recreational Cannabis Dispensaries in November
item.description: Mason residents will vote in November on whether to allow two recreational cannabis dispensaries in the city. If passed, Mason could see its first dispensaries open by early next year.

item.title: Michigan Supreme Court Considers Whether Cannabis Odor Justifies Vehicle Searches
item.description: The Michigan Supreme Court is evaluating whether the smell of cannabis can justify vehicle searches now that the substance is legal, raising questions about the distinction between lawful possession and illegal use.

item.title: Acme Township Rejects Cannabis Facility
item.description: Acme Township trustees denied a request to expand a medical cannabis facility

item.title: Lodi Township Residents to Vote on Limited Cannabis Cultivation
item.description: Lodi Township voters will decide on Proposal B this November, which could allow five cannabis growers and two processing facilities in the community. Retail operations would remain banned.

item.title: Cannabis Businesses Push Back Against Hemp-Derived THC Products
item.description: Michigan cannabis operators are rallying for a ban on CBD conversion oils, citing safety concerns and unfair competition. The issue has sparked intense debate within the industry and could shape the future of cannabis regulation in the state.

item.title: Kent County Deputies Recover Cannabis, Firearm After Brief Pursuit
item.description: A traffic stop in Gaines Township escalated into a brief police chase, ending with two arrests and the recovery of cannabis, cash, and a firearm. No injuries were reported.

item.title: Michigan Court Closes Loophole Allowing Unlicensed Cannabis Growers to Avoid Felonies
item.description: The Michigan Court of Appeals ruled that large-scale cannabis distribution without a license can result in felony charges, reversing a previous decision that limited penalties to misdemeanors. The ruling aims to curb illegal operations impacting the state’s cannabis market.

item.title: Proposal to Allow Cannabis Dispensaries in Howell Sparks Debate
item.description: A November ballot proposal could bring cannabis dispensaries to Howell, but residents and local officials remain divided on the issue, with health and community image at the center of the debate.

item.title: Stepping Back from MIMJNews - A Personal Farewell
item.description: Ryan, the sole writer and operator of MIMJNews, announces a heartfelt decision to step back from the site, citing family priorities and challenges with growth and visibility.
